title: Frontend: Character Counter
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Character Counter. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Count Unicode code points in Text, including spaces. Return {count,remaining} for a budget of 10; remaining clamps at zero, while count can exceed ten. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: Text. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Choose UTF-16 units, code points, or grapheme clusters explicitly because they produce different answers for emoji and combining marks.
alternativeApproaches: Support separate user-visible grapheme counts and server byte limits without conflating the two.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty text; pasted long text; emoji.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
